exercise.name: Barbell Suitcase Carry

reference.title: Barbell Suitcase Carry
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked from this environment); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (isometric grip, shoulder and trunk bracing while walking)

breathing.pattern: Brace and breathe behind the brace: short, steady breaths while you walk.
breathing.cadence: Steady steps, about 80-85 a minute here

prescription.progression: Longer distance, then more plates. Load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can carry with the trunk dead upright.

cues.text: Stand beside the barbell, hinge and grip it at its exact middle, then stand up tall; bar level and pointing forward, shoulders level, the free arm relaxed.
Walk with short, controlled steps; stay tall and do not lean toward or away from the bar.
Stop with the feet together, stay tall, then hinge to set the bar down; switch hands.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning toward or away from the bar
mistakes.fix: Brace and stay vertical; shoulders level.
Grip exactly at the middle (its balance point) and squeeze.
Pull the shoulder up and back to level with the free side.
Short, quiet steps keep the bar steady.

kinematics.peak: 50 cm steps (stride 100 cm), 100 cm per loop
kinematics.norm: Shorter than normal walking under heavy load (Winwood 2014, farmers walk)

kinematics.setup: ≈5° from vertical standing, no side bend
kinematics.peak: ≈5° mid-step; spine side-bend channels 0 (upright against the one-sided load)
kinematics.norm: Upright with no side bending toward or away from the load (Taylor & Reed 2020)

kinematics.setup: Held at its middle in the right hand, bar fore-aft, plates 54.6 cm off the floor
kinematics.peak: Within 1.5° of level and 0.3° of straight ahead; ≥8.2 cm from the body (rig shapes)
kinematics.norm: Held at its balance point, level, beside the leg (common coaching)

sources.title: GymVisual #22485, Barbell Suitcase Carry, video (movement reference)
Winwood, Cronin, Brown & Keogh 2014, a biomechanical analysis of the farmers walk, and comparison with the deadlift and unloaded walk (Int J Sports Sci Coach 9(5):1127-1143)
Taylor & Reed 2020, increase hip and trunk stability with loaded carries for injury prevention, rehabilitation, and performance (NSCA Coach 7(3))
The quantification of muscle activation during the loaded carry movement pattern, 2024 (Int J Exerc Sci 17(1):480-490; PubMed 38665162)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Clear a straight walking path; a long bar needs room in front and behind.
Pick up and set down the bar with a hip hinge and a flat back.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Grip gives out first: use a lighter bar or a dumbbell or kettlebell suitcase carry.
Back discomfort: lighter load, shorter distance.
regressions: Farmers carry with a dumbbell in each hand.

muscleNotes.obliques_l: Main target: the obliques on the side away from the bar resist the trunk bending toward the load (Taylor & Reed 2020; clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Co-contract with the far side to keep the trunk stiff (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the trunk upright and still against the one-sided load (Taylor & Reed 2020); trunk muscles were among the most active in loaded carries (loaded carry activation, 2024).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bar at its middle; a long bar also tries to tip forward or back, which the grip resists (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Steady the wrist so the bar stays level (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level while standing on the left leg with the load on the right (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level in the right-leg stance phases (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Resist the pull toward the loaded side together with the obliques (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the loaded shoulder level instead of letting it drop (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the loaded arm close to the side (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blade set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extension in each stance phase (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Push off at the end of each stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extension in each stance phase (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Push off at the end of each stance (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Stand tall, bar in the right hand
